one_line: Tamil Shaiva poet-saint of Madurai and Tirupperunturai, famed for the devotional hymns of the Thiruvasagam.

appearance.age_look: early 40s, lean and ascetic but healthy
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown Tamil complexion, sharp nose, gently arched brows, small neatly trimmed beard and moustache, large thoughtful eyes with a calm, inward-looking gaze and a serene half-smile as default expression
appearance.hair: shoulder-length wavy black hair parted slightly off-center, oiled and neatly combed back with a few loose strands, gathered into a low knot at the nape; simple white cotton headband tied around the crown, narrow and plain
appearance.costume: era-appropriate South Indian Shaiva brahmin attire: a full-length off-white cotton veshti/dhoti wrapped from waist to ankles with a neat front pleat and thin maroon border, worn high and secure; upper body covered by a soft, off-white cotton uttariya/angavastram draped over both shoulders and chest like a shawl, with subtle woven stripe near the edge; underneath, a pale cream long-sleeved cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh for modest layering; simple leather sandals; three horizontal sacred ash lines (vibhuti) and a small red tilaka on the forehead, plus vibhuti on arms and chest visible at collar; minimal jewellery—small gold stud earrings and a single rudraksha mala around the neck.
appearance.signature: a neatly rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a thin red cord, carried in his left hand or tucked under his arm, with one loose palm leaf held in his right hand as if reciting.

ref_desc: Manikkavachakar is a lean, medium-brown Tamil man in his early 40s with shoulder-length black hair, headband, vibhuti-marked serene face, off-white dhoti and shawl over a cream tunic, minimal rudraksha mala, sandals, and a maroon-tied palm-leaf manuscript bundle.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Manikkavachakar: a lean Tamil man in his early 40s with an oval, medium-brown face, large thoughtful eyes, small beard and moustache, and a calm half-smile. His shoulder-length wavy black hair is neatly combed back and gathered into a low knot, with a simple narrow white cotton headband around his crown. Three horizontal sacred ash lines and a small red tilaka mark his forehead, with faint vibhuti on his arms and upper chest at the collar. He wears era-accurate South Indian Shaiva brahmin clothing: a full-length off-white cotton veshti/dhoti with a thin maroon border, wrapped from waist to ankles with a clean front pleat; a pale cream long-sleeved cotton tunic underneath; and an off-white cotton uttariya/angavastram draped modestly over both shoulders and across his chest like a shawl, showing a subtle woven stripe near the edges. His feet are in simple brown leather sandals. Jewellery is minimal: small gold stud earrings and a single rudraksha mala around his neck. In his hands he holds his signature prop—a neatly rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a thin maroon-red cord, with one loose palm leaf in the other hand as if he is reciting. Use a restrained palette of off-white, cream, maroon, black, and warm brown, and present him front-facing with clear head-to-toe visibility for consistent redrawing.
